motivation: The earlier random-photo-first H5 analysis prospectively defined a negative scale-moderation hypothesis: climate-colour coupling may be stronger in geographically localized species and weaken as occupied geographic span increases. The new balanced RGFCA WorldClim edge analysis provides an independent larger species frame and a distance-controlled species-level climate-colour effect suitable for a direct replication.

response.name: species_partial_rho_colour_vs_worldclim_given_distance
response.definition: For each WorldClim-evaluable species, the equal-edge-occurrence partial Spearman correlation between ranked within-species colour-edge score and frozen multivariate WorldClim contrast after residualizing both on ranked great-circle edge distance, using the exact RGFCA 200-outer k=3 edge schedule.

moderator.name: mean_pairwise_H1_18x9_cell_centroid_great_circle_km
moderator.purpose: exact conceptual replication of the earlier H5 primary geographic-span moderator
construction: use the full frozen RGFCA classifiable photo pool, without reading colour values for the moderator
retain photos with complete frozen WorldClim coverage
assign photo coordinates to the legacy H1 18x9 equal-area longitude by sin(latitude) grid
within species take unique occupied H1 cells
require at least three occupied H1 cells
compute great-circle distances among all occupied-cell centroids
take the arithmetic mean of pairwise distances
apply log1p before the across-species rank correlation

primary_test.statistic: Spearman correlation across evaluable species between log1p(mean pairwise H1-cell geographic span) and species partial rho colour-vs-WorldClim-given-distance
primary_test.interpretation_if_negative: macroclimate-colour concordance weakens as a species spans broader geography, consistent with context dependence rather than one globally portable climate-colour mapping

null.unit: complete four-group colour vectors permuted within species
null.for_each_null: recompute each species WorldClim partial rho on the exact fixed edge schedule, then recompute the across-species scale-moderation Spearman statistic

support_rule.claim_if_supported: In the balanced global public-photo frame, the strength of distance-controlled macroclimate-flower-colour concordance is scale dependent: geographically broader species show weaker species-level climate-colour coupling under the frozen WorldClim representation. This is a replication-level association, not evidence that geographic range causes weaker selection or that climate causally determines flower colour.
support_rule.claim_if_not_supported: The larger balanced RGFCA frame does not replicate the earlier suggested weakening of climate-colour coupling with geographic span.
